experiment: TimeSeries unpatched ClickHouse vs VictoriaMetrics single-node same-runtime 50k series

measurement.p50_p95: client wall time including HTTP and JSON
measurement.similar_server_state: same cgroup, separate process and storage

limitations: Not patched ClickHouse results. The lab fast path binary is still compiling in GitHub Actions.
VM implements MetricsQL rate() semantics; ClickHouse implements PromQL rate() extrapolation; verify results, not just latency.
Synthetic counters are highly compressible and have no churn or concurrency; do not extrapolate absolute numbers to production.
Results came from consecutive engine runs with other workloads present in the shared container, not perfect isolated experimental control.
ClickHouse and VM apply different query planning and grid conversion; identify CPU/RSS and read_rows bottlenecks before drawing conclusions.
The same generated input samples were imported into both engines; the source code for regenerating input is in .github/ts-lab-bench/generate.py.
